newsitem.title: USA: Peru gains access to international capital markets.
newsitem.headline: Peru gains access to international capital markets.

text.p: Peru's completion of its external-debt financing plan will allow Peru access to the international capital markets, Peru's Economy Minister Jorge Camet and Citibank Vice Chairman William Rhodes said in a joint statement.

"With today's closing, Peru has attained its objective to further enhance its good standing with the international financial community. Peru will now be in a position to fully access the international capital and credit markets required to supplement its internal resources and finance its economic development into the next century," Camet said.
Peru's external debt financing covers an original principal amount of $4.3 billion in medium- and long-term commercial debt, the joint statement said.
Citibank's Rhodes said: "Peru has now normalized its relations with its commercial creditors, which will facilitate access to the international capital markets."
The financial instruments that were exchanged at today's closing in New York involved approximately 180 creditors, the statement said.

Under the plan, the Peruvian government issued today $560 million in discount bonds, $182 million in par bonds, $1.7 billion in front-loaded interest reduction bonds and $2.4 billion in past-due interest bonds.
The government also repurchased $2.6 billion of principal and past-due interest of eligible debt under a debt buyback.

The Bank Advisory Committee for Peru comprised of Citibank N.A., as chair, Bank of Nova Scotia, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi LTD, Bankers Trust Co, Banque National de Paris, Chase Manhattan Bank and Dresdner Bank AG.
